# gpg_key (Resource)

Manages an OpenPGP key in a gpg secrets engine mount.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gpg_key" "app" {
  backend   = "gpg"
  name      = "app"
  algorithm = "rsa-4096"
  identity  = "App <app@example.com>"
}

output "app_public_key" {
  value = gpg_key.app.public_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `backend` (String) Mount path of the gpg secrets engine (e.g. "gpg"). Changing this forces a new key.
- `name` (String) Name of the key. Changing this forces a new key.

### Optional

- `algorithm` (String) Key algorithm: rsa-2048, rsa-3072, rsa-4096 or ed25519. Defaults to rsa-3072. Changing this forces a new key.
- `deletion_allowed` (Boolean) Whether the key may be deleted. Terraform enables this automatically on destroy. Defaults to false.
- `exportable` (Boolean) Allow exporting the private key. Can be enabled later but never disabled. Defaults to false.
- `identity` (String) OpenPGP User ID (e.g. "Jane Doe <jane@example.com>"). Defaults to the key name. Changing this forces a new key.
- `min_decryption_version` (Number) Minimum key version usable for decryption. Must be between 1 and `latest_version`, otherwise the write fails. Defaults to 1.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprint` (String) OpenPGP fingerprint of the latest version.
- `key_id` (String) OpenPGP key ID of the latest version.
- `latest_version` (Number) The current (highest) key version.
- `public_key` (String) Armored public key of the latest version (import into gpg/pass to encrypt to this key).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <backend>/<name>.
terraform import gpg_key.app gpg/app
```
